```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(pollinatoR)
```

## From a ratio to a dollar figure

A dependence ratio says what share of a crop's yield is owed to pollinators.
Multiplied by the crop's production and price, it gives the value of that
pollination: the dependence-ratio method of Gallai et al. (2009). This
vignette takes a fitted estimand through to such a value, with an interval.
The value is computed for each draw of the estimand, and the interval comes
from the value draws.

Each printed value lists the estimand and its basis, the population, the
price year, the currency and the source of the market inputs.

## A simulated trial

The trial has three arms in twelve blocks: plants *bagged* against insects,
plants left *open*, and plants pollinated by *hand*. The blocks lie in canola
fields at three distances from native vegetation, four blocks per distance
band. Open plants yield less the further the field is from vegetation;
bagged and hand-pollinated plants do not depend on distance. The response is
seed yield per plant in grams.

```{r data}
set.seed(2025)
n_block <- 12L
n_plant <- 6L
blocks <- sprintf("B%02d", seq_len(n_block))
bands <- c("0-100 m", "100-300 m", "over 300 m")
band <- setNames(rep(bands, each = 4L), blocks)
trial <- expand.grid(
  plant = seq_len(n_plant),
  trt = c("Bagged", "Open", "Hand"),
  block = blocks,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
trial$band <- band[trial$block]
block_effect <- setNames(rnorm(n_block, 0, 0.1), blocks)
open_mean <- setNames(c(2.4, 2.1, 1.8), bands)
arm_mean <- ifelse(
  trial$trt == "Bagged",
  1.4,
  ifelse(trial$trt == "Hand", 2.6, open_mean[trial$band])
)
mu <- arm_mean * exp(block_effect[trial$block])
trial$yield <- rgamma(nrow(trial), shape = 25, rate = 25 / mu)

pd <- pollin_data(trial, response = "yield", treatment = "trt", unit = "block")
ds <- pollin_design(
  pd,
  arms = c(excluded = "Bagged", open = "Open", supplemented = "Hand"),
  layout = "rcbd"
)
```

## A population of distance bands

The trial's blocks are not a sample of the district's canola. Suppose a land
use map shows 300 ha of canola within 100 m of native vegetation, 500 ha at
100 to 300 m and 1,200 ha beyond. `pollin_population()` declares the bands as
strata weighted by those areas.

```{r population}
district <- pollin_population(
  "band",
  c("0-100 m" = 300, "100-300 m" = 500, "over 300 m" = 1200),
  label = "district canola, by distance to vegetation"
)
district
```

The estimand takes the population, and fitting with the bands as `by` gives
each band its own treatment effect.

```{r estimand}
dep <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss", population = district)
fit_dep <- pollin_fit(dep, by = "band")
```

## Draws of the estimand

`pollin_draws()` draws the fixed effects from their sampling distribution and
recomputes the expected yield in each arm for every draw. The loss share is
formed from each pair of arm means. A further column holds the population:
the area-weighted arm means, and the loss share formed from them.

```{r draws}
dr_dep <- pollin_draws(fit_dep, n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
dr_dep
summary(dr_dep)[, c("level", "median", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
```

The planted loss shares are 0.42, 0.33 and 0.22 in the three bands. The
population loss share is a ratio of population means,
$1 - \sum w\,\mathrm{low} / \sum w\,\mathrm{high}$, and so weights each band by
its area and its open yield.

## Market inputs

`pollin_market()` records current production and its price. Current production
means the crop as it is pollinated now, the open arm in the trial's terms.
The figures below are illustrative.

```{r market}
canola <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 3600,
  price = 700,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "canola"
)
canola
```

## The dependence channel

`pollin_value()` needs a channel; there is no default. The `dependence`
channel values the production that would be lost if pollinators were wholly
excluded.

```{r value-dep}
val_dep <- pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence")
val_dep
```

The value is computed per draw as $D \times P \times Q$, with
$D = 1 - \mathrm{excluded}/\mathrm{open}$. Production without pollinators
would be $Q \times \mathrm{excluded}/\mathrm{open}$, a loss of $D \times Q$.

Price and production are rarely known exactly. They can be given as draws,
one per estimand draw, matched by position.

```{r value-draws}
set.seed(7)
canola_unc <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 3600,
  price = 700,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs with uncertainty",
  quantity_draws = rlnorm(1000L, log(3600), 0.10),
  price_draws = rlnorm(1000L, log(700), 0.15),
  crop = "canola"
)
summary(pollin_value(dr_dep, canola_unc, channel = "dependence"))[
  , c("median", "conf.low", "conf.high", "currency")
]
```

The median barely moves. The interval is wider because price and
production are now uncertain too.

## The deficit channel

The `deficit` channel values the yield lost because the crop's pollination
falls short of hand pollination: the gain if every plant were pollinated as
well as by hand. It needs a supplemented arm, and a deficit estimand with
`basis = "gain"`.

```{r value-deficit}
def <- pollin_estimand(ds, "deficit", "ratio", "gain", population = district)
dr_def <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(def, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
pollin_value(dr_def, canola, channel = "deficit")
```

Here the value per draw is
$(\mathrm{hand}/\mathrm{open} - 1) \times P \times Q$, the gain over current
production. In both channels the ratio is taken relative to the open arm,
because $Q$ is open-pollinated production. That is why each channel accepts
one ratio only: a loss share for `dependence` and a gain for `deficit`.

## Why the dependence channel refuses a gain

The loss share $D$ and the gain $g = \mathrm{open}/\mathrm{excluded} - 1$ come
from the same two arm means, and $g = D/(1 - D)$. A gain multiplied by
current production overstates the loss by the factor $1/(1 - D)$, so the
dependence channel refuses it.

```{r refuse-gain, error = TRUE}
dep_gain <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "gain", population = district)
dr_gain <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(dep_gain, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
try(pollin_value(dr_gain, canola, channel = "dependence"))
```

A descriptive index from `pollin_index()` or a plain number is refused as
well, because neither records the estimand it came from.

## Sensitivity: two populations

The area weights are an input, and a different map gives a different value.
To see how much, value the estimand under a second population and compare. Here a second population puts
most of the canola close to vegetation.

```{r sensitivity}
near <- pollin_population(
  "band",
  c("0-100 m" = 1000, "100-300 m" = 600, "over 300 m" = 400),
  label = "canola mostly near vegetation"
)
dep_near <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss", population = near)
dr_near <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(dep_near, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
rbind(
  summary(pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence")),
  summary(pollin_value(dr_near, canola, channel = "dependence"))
)[, c("median", "conf.low", "conf.high", "currency")]
```

The first row is the district map, the second the map with most canola near
vegetation. With production held at 3,600 t, the second value is higher,
because the crop near vegetation loses a larger share without pollinators.

## Adding values without counting twice

Values can be added only when they count different things.
`pollin_guard_doublecount()` adds values draw by draw and stops when two of
them overlap. It compares the pollinators each exclusion removed (`agent`, all
of them here), the product valued and the crop.

The value of canola seed and the value of the oil pressed from it are not
separate contributions: the oil's value includes the seed's. The guard
refuses the sum.

```{r guard-refuse, error = TRUE}
oil <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 1500,
  price = 1600,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "canola"
)
try(pollin_guard_doublecount(
  seed = pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence", product = "seed"),
  oil = pollin_value(dr_dep, oil, channel = "dependence", product = "oil")
))
```

Values for two crops, each from its own trial, do not overlap. A second
small trial in faba bean gives a second value, and the guard adds the two.

```{r guard-allow}
set.seed(11)
faba_trial <- expand.grid(
  plant = seq_len(6L),
  trt = c("Bagged", "Open"),
  block = sprintf("F%d", seq_len(8L)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
faba_mu <- ifelse(faba_trial$trt == "Open", 30, 24)
faba_trial$yield <- rgamma(nrow(faba_trial), shape = 20, rate = 20 / faba_mu)
faba_ds <- pollin_design(
  pollin_data(faba_trial, "yield", "trt", unit = "block"),
  c(excluded = "Bagged", open = "Open"),
  "rcbd"
)
faba_dr <- pollin_draws(
  pollin_fit(pollin_estimand(faba_ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")),
  n = 1000L,
  seed = 2L
)
faba <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 900,
  price = 450,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "faba bean"
)
pollin_guard_doublecount(
  canola = pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence", product = "seed"),
  faba = pollin_value(faba_dr, faba, channel = "dependence", product = "seed")
)
```

## What the value assumes

Each printed value lists its assumptions:

* No price response. The price is held fixed, although losing a large share
  of a crop's production would raise its price.
* A total-loss counterfactual, for the dependence channel. The value is the
  production lost if every pollinator were removed, with nothing in their
  place. It is not the loss from a partial decline.
* Independence of the estimand and the market draws. A season that is poor
  for pollination may also be a season of high prices; the draws are paired
  as if the two were unrelated.

Within each stratum of a population, the trial's expected yields are taken to
hold across the stratum's area, and the areas are taken as exact.

The value is gross: the revenue from the production at stake, before any
costs. The default simulation draws take the fixed effects and the trial's
own block effects jointly, so the interval covers the uncertainty in both. It
does not cover new blocks drawn afresh; `pollin_draws()` with
`method = "bootstrap"` includes those, at the cost of refitting the model.

## References

Gallai, N., Salles, J.-M., Settele, J., & Vaissière, B. E. (2009). Economic
valuation of the vulnerability of world agriculture confronted with
pollinator decline. *Ecological Economics*, *68*(3), 810--821.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolecon.2008.06.014
